findings.title: Materials' 53-point lens gap signals peak-cycle earnings
findings.body: Materials trades at 17.26x forward versus 38.38x trailing, a 53-point percentile gap between the two lenses. That is the market pricing a 122 percent earnings rebound while trailing earnings sit at the 93rd percentile of five years, an unusual combination that suggests analysts expect current margins to be a cyclical high.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' cheap forward hides rich trailing
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward P/E sits at the 51st percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 89th, a 38-point gap. The 33 percent multiple compression implies a 48 percent earnings jump, but that is a heavy bet on margin recovery for a sector whose trailing valuation has rarely been this expensive.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward percentile lags trailing
findings.body: Information Technology's trailing P/E is at the 70th percentile but its forward multiple is at the 24th, a 46-point gap. The 42 percent compression assumes 71 percent earnings growth, yet the forward percentile is near a five-year low, meaning the market is already discounting a steep profit surge that has not materialized.
